we present a generative model for incremental class learning that is memory efficient, inspired by brain mechanisms, and outperforms state of the art methods.

we propose a novel generative deep network model, FearNet, for incremental class learning, that uses a brain inspired memory architecture, that does not store examples from previous classes, that uses a novel module inspired by the amygdala to select which memory system to recall from, that achieves state of the-art performance on incremental class learning on CIFAR 100, AudioSet and CUB 200 benchmarks, and that outperforms iCaRL by a significant margin on the AudioSet benchmark.

the problem of learning from data that is sequentially presented in batches.
developing a model that can learn new classes in bursts of data without catastrophic forgetting.
